scope: Exploratory matched saved-read token deletion on seq11 and inset-excluded seq23, with snapshots fixed before this analysis. Seq8 and seq20 are not included in this initial fixed-read study. No new video propagation, detector call, or labels during scoring and replay.
hypothesis: A trained prompt-conditioned early-feature channel gate may rank useful historical memory tokens differently from usage and unweighted contrast under an identical deletion budget.
reconstruction: Re-encode the saved automatic-prompt image and the exact source images using the verified Lean CPU FP32 image encoder and video-loader resize and normalization. Reconstruct unweighted contrast at each captured source token. Abort unless it matches the saved unweighted contrast within a prespecified absolute tolerance of 1e-6, with identical token identities and crop geometry. No labels are read.
arms: No-op; usage; existing unweighted contrast; distributed across frames; RGB contrast; deterministic shuffled unweighted contrast; three-region; and prompt-conditioned, descriptor-independent, and mismatched-descriptor trained author-CBAM gates. Mismatched descriptors come from seq9, held fixed for both tested sequences. All deletion arms remove exactly 1024 eligible historical tokens from the same read and protect prompt and object pointers. Source uses the original captured usage ranks and token IDs.
validation: Repeat reconstructed score generation and replay in independent processes, verify source/prompt/checkpoint/code hashes, baseline equality, mask hashes and equal attention key counts. Open labels only after both replays; compute per-frame present Dice and labeled-empty false alarms against the no-op and controls. Local deletion effects do not establish closed-loop efficacy or patient-independent generalization.
limitations: The tiny training set and validation results do not support a full-video candidate; this is a different causal token-utility diagnostic. Seq11 and seq23 have already been inspected and are exploratory. Because the model was trained on a feature-ranking surrogate, positive fixed-read results alone do not authorize deployment.
